raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t chase fancy ways. On my 4.1 mu I will still do wheat and then maize, same as before. This land feeds us and gives us cash, and wheat-maize is the safest here. I watch what the neighbors do. If the year starts normal, I sow wheat in early October after cleaning the field, then harvest in early June and put maize in right away. I have a well, so I will use water, but not too many times because pumping costs money. For fertilizer, I won’t use too little because if the crop turns weak, the loss is bigger than saving a little cash. But I also won’t push too hard at my age and on such a small plot. I’ll use a moderate amount, mostly the same as years when the crop looked steady.

For wheat, I’ll use ordinary improved seed from the local dealer, put most fertilizer before sowing, then add some urea when the wheat starts to stand up strong in spring. I’ll water around sowing if the soil is dry, then again at jointing and maybe once around filling if the season is dry. For maize, there is no time to waste after wheat harvest, so I will turn the land lightly or hire a small machine if needed and plant quickly. I’ll use hybrid maize seed, put base fertilizer once, then topdress once when the maize is knee high. If rain is not enough, I’ll water once or twice. I only spray pesticide if I see weeds or insects; I don’t like spending money before I have to.
